rfi.title: France marks 10 years since Bastille Day terror attack in Nice killed 86
rfi.description: Religious leaders have gathered in Nice for an interfaith service to pray for the victims of the Bastille Day terror attack, on the eve of the 10th anniversary of the atrocity that killed 86 people and injured more than 400. President Emmanuel Macron is due to lead the main memorial ceremony later on Tuesday, while a minute's silence will be observed before France's World Cup semi-final against Spain.

rfi.title: Fifty-nine arrested over wildfires, including two for Fontainebleau blaze near Paris
rfi.description: A total of 59 people have been arrested across France over suspected deliberate or accidental arson, including two in connection with the wildfire still sweeping through the Fontainebleau forest southeast of Paris, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said.

rfi.title: Ukraine's allies pledge jets, missiles and anti-ballistic shield at Paris summit
rfi.description: Ukraine's allies announced additional air defence support for Kyiv at a summit in Paris on Monday, along with exercises for the force to be deployed after a ceasefire, as part of efforts to increase pressure on Russia to end the war.

rfi.title: France, Spain collide for World Cup final berth with Deschamps chasing history
rfi.description: France's attack led by Kylian Mbappe take on a technically accomplished Spain team in the first semi-final of the World Cup on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Paris balls cancelled amid heatwave as 14 July marks 10 years since Nice
rfi.description: Bastille Day firefighters' balls in Paris and the surrounding suburbs have been cancelled owing to record-high temperatures affecting the capital and most of France, as emergency workers remain on alert. Celebrations begin on Monday, with Paris having brought forward its annual fireworks display by a day to avoid clashing with commemorations marking the 10th anniversary of the Nice attack of 14 July 2016.

rfi.title: France, Germany, UK condemn Iran attacks as renewed fighting with US puts peace deal at risk
rfi.description: The foreign ministers of France, Germany, and Britain have condemned Iran's attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on countries in the region, as Iran and the United States have traded attacks in recent days, casting doubt on their interim agreement to end the war.

rfi.title: Mbappé, Dembélé, Olise dazzle up front but Maignan makes it possible
rfi.description: France's attacking trio - Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé and Michael Olise - have dominated the World Cup headlines, scoring plenty of goals and dazzling fans with skilful moves and fast breaks past opposing defences. Meanwhile, at the other end of the pitch, goalkeeper Mike Maignan has laid the foundation that's made all that attacking flair possible.

rfi.title: Ukraine's allies gather in Paris as Kremlin dismisses 'coalition of warmongers'
rfi.description: Allies of Ukraine gathered in Paris on Monday alongside President Volodymyr Zelensky to reaffirm their support for Kyiv and step up pressure on Russia, at a summit of the so-called "Coalition of the Willing" that the Kremlin promptly dismissed as a meeting of leaders who "do not want peace".

rfi.title: France to summon Russian ambassador over cyber attacks
rfi.description: France will summon the Russian ambassador to Paris over an alleged Russian cyberhacking campaign against European countries including France, as the EU and Britain targeted Russia with coordinated sanctions.

rfi.title: Record 128 migrants cross Channel in one boat as overall numbers drop
rfi.description: A small boat carrying 128 people has reached the coast of England, marking a new record for the largest single crossing of the Channel on a small boat, even as the number of crossings has dropped in recent months.

rfi.title: Experts to deliver verdict on EU social media controls for children
rfi.description: An expert committee is due to deliver its recommendations on Monday on how the European Union should regulate children's access to social media, including a potential blanket ban. More than 20 countries worldwide, including France, have already implemented or proposed age restrictions.

rfi.title: Massive fire burns in Fontainebleau near Paris
rfi.description: Firefighers are mobilised in the Fontainebleau forest south of Paris to contain a major fire that started Sunday and has since forced the evacuation of residents in the area and shut down a major highway at the start of a busy summer holiday travel weekend.

rfi.title: Trump lifts Turkey sanctions, eyes F-35 sale
rfi.description: US President Donald Trump made headlines this week at the Nato summit in Ankara by declaring an end to all sanctions against Turkey, paving the way for the sale of the F-35 stealth fighter jet to the alarm of Greece and Israel.

rfi.title: Spain braced to face France's firepower in World Cup semi-final
rfi.description: Spain will attempt to neutralise one of the most potent attacking arsenals in World Cup history on Tuesday when they take on France in a heavyweight semi-final showdown.

rfi.title: China's missile test overshadowed by Iran war, but Pacific nations are watching
rfi.description: China recenly test-fired a nuclear-capable missile from a submarine into the Pacific, the first such launch from a nuclear-powered vessel and the first submarine-based test since 1982.

rfi.title: France remembers 'old demons' of antisemitism on first annual Dreyfus day
rfi.description: Sunday saw France observe its first annual day of commemoration for Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish army officer wrongly convicted of treason in one of the country's most notorious cases of antisemitism. With reports of hate speech on the rise, President Emmanuel Macron said France had yet to shed its "old demons" of prejudice.

rfi.title: In Zimbabwe, community seed banks are reviving indigenous crops
rfi.description: Zimbabwean farmers are reviving drought-resistant traditional crops through a community seed bank, helping them cope with worsening climate variability. The initiative, rooted in indigenous knowledge, is strengthening food security and offering a safety net against future droughts and floods.

rfi.title: China's rising foie gras industry has France looking over its shoulder
rfi.description: China has risen rapidly to become the world's second-largest producer of foie gras, but producers in France say they are not yet worried about losing their long-held dominance of one of the country's best-known delicacies.

euronews.title: First Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine to start human trials in the UK
euronews.description: Scientists in Oxford will start to test the world's first vaccine against Bundibugyo Ebola, as an outbreak of the rare virus strain continues to spread across Congo and Uganda.

euronews.title: Street artists from 21 countries transform Oslo into an open-air graffiti gallery
euronews.description: Oslo’s former industrial district became an open-air gallery as 40 artists from 21 countries painted murals over three days at one of the largest street art festivals of its kind.

euronews.title: Almost 60 people gored or bruised during Spain's famed San Fermín bull runs
euronews.description: Sixteen people have been killed in the bull runs since records started in 1911. The last death was in 2009 when a bull gored a 27-year-old Spaniard in the neck, heart and lungs.

euronews.title: Yamal replies to Rajoy's Les Bleus column: 'Football should unite society'
euronews.description: Spain's former prime minister used a TV debate to question the origins of several France players at the 2026 World Cup. Asked about it before the semi-final, Lamine Yamal sidestepped the row and hailed football as a model of integration.

euronews.title: 'Digger': Is this the movie that finally wins Tom Cruise his first competitive Oscar?
euronews.description: Tom Cruise leads Oscar-winning director Alejandro González Iñárritu’s forthcoming satirical comedy - and from the trailer alone, it’s clear that the actor’s transformative turn is vying for Oscar glory.

euronews.title: Fact check: FIFA boss Infantino probe called for by MEPs, not whole parliament
euronews.description: Viral posts falsely claim that the European Parliament called for an investigation into FIFA's President Gianni Infantino.

euronews.title: Fontainebleau fire still burning as 850 firefighters tackle blaze
euronews.description: The fire in the Fontainebleau forest, around sixty kilometres from Paris, is still spreading. Around 850 firefighters, 200 vehicles and six aircraft have been deployed.

euronews.title: Fairmont’s new English lakeside resort has a Gordon Ramsay restaurant, spa and golf course
euronews.description: Located in England’s northwest, the new Fairmont Cheshire, The Mere is a luxury countryside resort with 116 rooms and suites, a Gordon Ramsay restaurant, an 18-hole championship-level golf course plus spa and wellness experiences.

euronews.title: 'We will deal with it,' Trump says as US probes reports of Iranian drones in Cuba
euronews.description: The US president said his administration is checking whether Tehran stores drones and missiles on the island and warned Washington will act if confirmed, but he offered no proof or details about the alleged weapons.

euronews.title: Ukraine inches closer towards joining EU with opening of another cluster
euronews.description: Ministers in Brussels approved the opening of another portion of Ukrainian accession negotiations on Tuesday. The decision continues the erosion of a two-year deadlock caused by the former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

euronews.title: Targeting Patriarch Kirill risks fuelling EU scepticism, Bulgarian foreign minister warns
euronews.description: Velislava Petrova-Chamova told Euronews that the EU’s sanctions against Russia should have a financial impact and not be a symbolic instrument – and that this, among other reasons, is why Sofia championed the removal of the head of Russia's Orthodox Church from the 21st sanctions package.

euronews.title: Sugar in space? Astronomers find sweet clue to the origin of life
euronews.description: It turns out the universe has something of a sweet tooth. Astronomers have detected a new type of sugar floating in deep space that may hold clues to how life first emerged on Earth.

euronews.title: ICE agent shoots dead Colombian immigrant in Maine
euronews.description: The 26-year-old, who had permission to work in the US, was killed in Biddeford when an officer opened fire, saying his car was a threat. It is the ninth death tied to Trump’s migration crackdown.

euronews.title: King’s Swan Upping on the Thames shows healthy cygnets but rising litter
euronews.description: Traditional skiffs glided along the River Thames during Swan Upping as crews counted and weighed cygnets, reporting encouraging numbers while warning about the growing threat of river litter.

euronews.title: France flaunts firepower and unity with allies as Macron hosts final Bastille Day parade
euronews.description: With nearly 6,700 troops, 98 aircraft, 31 helicopters and 315 vehicles, a record number of military personnel were marching the traditional route between the Arc de Triomphe and the Place de la Concorde.

euronews.title: US releases video of sea drone strike on Iranian naval base
euronews.description: The US military has released video it says shows three Corsair unmanned surface vessels striking a ship maintenance facility and submarine at Iran's Bandar Abbas Naval Base on 12 July. US Central Command says it was the first combat use of American sea drones.

euronews.title: Flowers and forensic teams at Bangkok bar where deadly fire killed at least 27
euronews.description: At least 27 people died and around 70 were injured in a bar fire in Bangkok, as police probe blocked exits and faulty wiring in the 50-year-old venue.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, 14-Juillet : Emmanuel Macron passe en revue les troupes le long des Champs-Elysées pour son dernier défilé
lemonde.description: Le défilé, qui prend place sur l’avenue des Champs-Elysées, entre l’Arc de triomphe et la place de la Concorde, est placé sous le signe du « réveil stratégique de l’Europe », dans un contexte de menaces sur le front est et de désengagement américain.

lemonde.title: A Fontainebleau, « plus les heures passent, plus ça devient irréel de se dire que la forêt est en flammes »
lemonde.description: Plus de 1 900 hectares avaient déjà été parcourus par le feu au matin du mardi 14 juillet. Des Canadair, des Dash et des hélicoptères bombardiers d’eau ont pour la première fois été engagés en Ile-de-France.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : un pétrolier touché par un missile au large d’Oman lundi, rapporte l’agence de sécurité maritime britannique
lemonde.description: « Un pétrolier a déclaré avoir été touché par un missile alors qu’il quittait le détroit [d’Ormuz] par la route du sud », a fait savoir l’UKMTO. Le commandement américain pour le Moyen-Orient a par ailleurs annoncé que les Etats-Unis reprendraient mardi à 22 heures le blocus des ports iraniens, qui avait été levé le 18 juin dans le cadre de la trêve entre Washington et Téhéran.

lemonde.title: DP World, l’entreprise qui a fait des Emirats arabes unis une puissance portuaire et logistique
lemonde.description: « La ruée sur les ports » (5/16). Majoritairement détenue par le gouvernement de Dubaï, la compagnie est présente dans 75 pays, jusqu’en Afrique et en Amérique du Sud. Elle est le bras armé des Emirats arabes unis pour sécuriser leurs approvisionnements en minerais ou en denrées agricoles.

lemonde.title: France-Espagne : des retrouvailles pour une affiche aux airs de « finale avant l’heure » dans la Coupe du monde 2026
lemonde.description: Pour la première fois depuis le début du Mondial, les Bleus rencontrent un adversaire à leur mesure en demi-finales de la compétition. La Roja affiche une confiance née de son titre européen acquis en 2024 et de ses deux dernières victoires face à la France.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Russie a lancé 135 drones et 10 missiles contre le territoire ukrainien pendant la nuit
lemonde.description: Des déflagrations ont retenti mardi peu après minuit à Kiev. Dans la région d’Odessa, des infrastructures industrielles ont été prises pour cible. Les frappes russes nocturnes ont également tué deux personnes dans la région de Dnipropetrovsk et en ont blessé quatre autres.

lemonde.title: Dix ans après l’attentat du 14-Juillet, Nice confrontée à un douloureux travail de mémoire
lemonde.description: Pour la ville, il est difficile de représenter l’horreur qui a fait 86 morts et plus de 400 blessés en 2016. Beaucoup de victimes ont l’impression de commémorations de « seconde zone ».

lemonde.title: Mengistu, le « Négus rouge » éthiopien, fantôme d’Harare
lemonde.description: « Chefs d’Etat africains en exil » (2/6). Autrefois colonel tout-puissant de la junte militaire éthiopienne, l’ancien despote Mengistu Hailé Mariam, aujourd’hui âgé de 89 ans, se terre depuis trente-cinq ans dans une villa cossue de la capitale zimbabwéenne.

lemonde.title: Tour de France 2026 : le parcours de la dixième étape (Aurillac-Le Lioran)
lemonde.description: En ce mardi 14 juillet, le Cantal est à la fête. Les coureurs français auront à cœur de briller sur un parcours très montagneux, qui pourrait inspirer aussi les leaders du classement général.

lemonde.title: « L’Europe, par la taille de son marché et son influence réglementaire, projette ses normes au-delà de ses frontières »
lemonde.description: Comme le montre l’exemple des viandes brésiliennes, les normes sanitaires et la traçabilité deviennent des variables centrales du commerce international et du risque économique pour les pays émergents, constate l’économiste brésilien Gustavo Pessoa, dans une tribune au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Paul et Denise Poiret, splendeurs et misères d’un couple d’avant-garde
lemonde.description: « Couture et déchirures » (2/6). Les histoires d’amour ou d’amitié finissent parfois mal. Y compris dans le milieu de la mode. Le coup de foudre du flamboyant couturier pour sa discrète muse sera à l’origine d’une véritable révolution esthétique au début du XXᵉ siècle. Et si, dans les années 1920, le couple ne survit pas aux difficultés financières, Denise restera toujours fidèle à la mémoire du créateur déchu.

lemonde.title: Mariage dans un château : comment prouver que les lieux étaient sales
lemonde.description: Les attestations de témoins produites par les mariés ont davantage de valeur que l’état des lieux « photographique » établi par le bailleur.

lemonde.title: « Cette folle envie de tuer », premier roman de Camilla Barnes, se tient entre légèreté drolatique et mélancolie
lemonde.description: Les rapports difficiles entre les membres d’une famille britannique installée en France donnent lieu a des quiproquos en tous genres.

lemonde.title: Olivier Rousteing, nouveau directeur artistique de Rabanne
lemonde.description: L’ancien designer de Balmain rejoint la maison du groupe Puig. Sa mode glamour et spectaculaire devrait s’accorder avec l’univers des parfums, moteur économique de Rabanne.

lemonde.title: Les brèves critiques du « Monde des livres » : Chico Buarque, Arnaud Cathrine, Hadrien Laroche, Alejandra Pizarnik…
lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, une sélection de parutions récentes, au-delà des titres phares.

lemonde.title: En Argentine, un théâtre si vivant
lemonde.description: Buenos Aires s’affirme comme l’épicentre d’un théâtre hispanophone créatif, aux propositions aussi précaires qu’abondantes, caractérisées par un jeu généreux.

france24fr.title: "Mbappé dictateur" : comment le capitaine des Bleus a tourné la critique en atout
france24fr.description: Depuis le début de la Coupe du monde, une tendance sur les réseaux sociaux associant Kylian Mbappé à l'image d'un dictateur tout-puissant a gagné en popularité sur internet et dans les stades. Si ce surnom visait à l'origine à critiquer l'autoritarisme supposé du capitaine des Bleus, il prend une toute autre signification avant d'affronter l'Espagne mardi à Dallas.

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine force la Russie à rediriger son trafic maritime en mer d'Azov
france24fr.description: L'armée ukrainienne a indiqué avoir frappé plus d'une centaine de bateaux russes en mer d'Azov, dont 11 dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, dans ce passage de transport stratégique pour les produits agricoles à destination de la Crimée, occupée par l'armée de Moscou. Kremlin étudie des routes alternatives.

france24fr.title: Un monde moins peuplé et plus âgé : l'hiver démographique
france24fr.description: En 2050, la Terre comptera 9,8 milliards d'habitants. Certains pays gagneront des habitants, d'autres en perdront. Les premiers se trouvent surtout parmi les nations en développement, les seconds parmi les pays développés. Quelles leçons en tirer ? Faut-il encourager la natalité au Nord et la freiner au Sud ? Quels leviers concrets pour agir sans normer les choix de vie ? Éléments de réponse avec nos deux invités.

france24fr.title: Léopards congolais au Mondial : à la découverte des ateliers de couture
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, c’est l’histoire d’une véritable success story : celle de la veste portée par les Léopards à leur arrivée aux États-Unis pour la Coupe du monde. Une création imaginée par un jeune styliste congolais et entièrement fabriquée à Kinshasa. Reportage d’Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Interdiction de l'alcool en sachet Nigeria : une mesure appliquée ?
france24fr.description: Au Nigeria, les sachets d’alcool auraient dû disparaître des étals. Interdits depuis fin 2025 pour limiter notamment la consommation chez les mineurs, ils restent pourtant largement vendus dans le pays. Entre difficultés d’application de la loi, enjeux économiques et préoccupations de santé publique, le commerce se poursuit.

france24fr.title: Au Soudan, le chef des FSR, le général Hemedti, condamné par contumace
france24fr.description: Au Soudan, la justice vient de condamner à mort par contumace le chef des Forces de Soutien Rapide, le général Hemedti. Selon la cour, il est responsable de crimes de guerre, crimes contre humanité et génocide, en particulier dans la région du Darfour Occidental.

france24fr.title: Meurtre d'une fillette au Cameroun : fermeture de 1 400 églises de réveil
france24fr.description: Au Cameroun, le ministre de l’Administration territoriale annonce la fermeture prochaine de 1 400 églises de réveil à travers le pays. Cette annonce intervient quelques jours après le meurtre à Yaoundé d'une fillette de 11 ans. L'auteure présumée du crime, fidèle d'une de ces églises, avait déclaré avoir agi sous l'influence d'un responsable religieux.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Pape Thiaw limogé après le Mondial
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal c'est l'heure comptes après l'élimination controversée des Lions de la Teranga à la Coupe du monde 2026. La Fédération Sénégalaise de Football qui s'est séparé du sélectionneur national Pape Thiaw pour des raisons sportives s'est expliquée ce lundi face à la presse.

france24fr.title: Le Slip français entre en bourse, un pari sur le "Made in France"
france24fr.description: La marque emblématique du fabriqué en France fait son entrée en bourse, ce 14 juillet. Un symbole pour une industrie textile qui tente de se réinventer le "Made in France" après des décennies de délocalisations et face à une concurrence asiatique toujours plus forte.

france24fr.title: Pakistan : la vallée du Hunza, joyau touristique, menacée par le réchauffement climatique
france24fr.description: Ces dernières décennies, la vallée de Hunza, dans le Gilgit-Baltistan, région montagneuse du nord du Pakistan, a connu une mutation spectaculaire : accès élargi à l’éducation, amélioration du système de santé et développement local. La construction d’hôtels et d’infrastructures s’est accélérée et la bétonisation devient de plus en plus visible dans certaines vallées. Mais le Gilgit Baltistan est en première ligne face au changement climatique. Des milliers de glaciers reculent, fragilisant cette

france24fr.title: 14-Juillet : "être ici c'est assez fantastique" pour ce Capitaine de l'artillerie de Marine
france24fr.description: Près de 6 700 troupes à pied, 98 avions, 31 hélicoptères et 315 véhicules : jamais autant de militaires n'auront défilé sur les Champs-Elysées afin d'illustrer "le réarmement de la France, l'autonomie stratégique de la France et le réveil stratégique européen", selon l'Elysée. Au micro de Mélina Huet pour France 24, le Capitaine Baudoin, 11ème régiment d'artillerie de Marine, "encourage tout ceux qui regardent le défilé à découvrir leur vocation".

france24fr.title: Pourquoi les Champs-Élysées s'appellent-ils... "Champs-Élysées" ?
france24fr.description: C'est un nom emblématique de Paris et du luxe, scène du défilé militaire du 14-Juillet comme des festivités de fin d'année. Mais savez-vous pourquoi la plus belle avenue du monde s'appelle "les Champs-Élysées" ?

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis frappent à nouveau l'Iran et menace d'imposer un blocus dans le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Au Moyen-Orient, Donald Trump monte d'un cran et menace de rétablir le blocus naval dans le détroit d'Ormuz demain soir. Les États-Unis ont encore pilonné des dizaines de cibles iraniennes la nuit dernière. En représailles, l'Iran a de nouveau frappé la Jordanie, Bahreïn et le Koweït. Les cours du pétrole se sont envolés de plus de 9%.

france24fr.title: Attentat de Nice : 10 ans plus tard, cérémonie de commémoration
france24fr.description: C'était il y a 10 ans, le 14 juillet 2016. La promenade des Anglais à Nice a été le théâtre d'un attentat sanglant. Au volant d'un camion de 19 tonnes, un homme de 31 ans a foncé sur la foule rassemblée pour la fête nationale faisant, 86 morts et plus de 450 blessés. Retour sur les faits avec Alice Brogat et Marc Paupe.

france24fr.title: Espagne : le bilan de l'incendie en Andalousie s'alourdit à treize morts, dont une française
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sánchez s'est rendu lundi sur les lieux de l'un des incendies les plus meurtriers de l'histoire récente du pays. Le bilan est lourd : au moins treize personnes ont perdu la vie, dont quatre Britanniques et une Française. Les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver d’éventuelles autres victimes. Certaines familles de disparus affirment ne pas avoir reçu d'ordre d'évacuation de la part des autorités. Les précisions de Marion Meyer.

france24fr.title: 8% de la forêt de Fontainebleau a déjà brûlé, 600 pompiers toujours mobilisés
france24fr.description: Les incendies qui font rage depuis dimanche après-midi dans la forêt de Fontainebleau ont parcouru plus de 1 900 hectares mardi matin, selon les pompiers de Seine-et-Marne. Cela correspond à plus de 8% de la forêt. Les chiffres, qui datent du milieu de la nuit, devraient évoluer dans la journée alors que le feu continue de progresser. Précisions d’Alexandra Quarini, journaliste France 24.

france24fr.title: Quand le défilé militaire du 14 juillet... n'était pas sur les Champs-Élysées
france24fr.description: C'est une parade que le monde entier envie à la France... et une partie de son succès vient de ce qu'elle se déroule sur la plus belle avenue du monde. Mais saviez-vous que le défilé militaire du 14 juillet n'avait pas toujours été organisé sur les Champs-Élysées ?

france24fr.title: 🔴 Incendies de Fontainebleau : plus de 1 900 hectares de forêt sont déjà partis en fumée

Notfälle: Pfleger nach Tigerangriff nahe Leipzig gestorben
Gedenken: Ahrtal-Jahrestag: «Eine Nacht, die ein Land nicht vergisst»
Schokoeisbecher mit Balsamico-Kirschen: Balsam(ico) für die Seele
zeit.description: Die drei besten Begleiter für Kirschen: Schokolade, Bananensaft und Balsamico. Zwei davon landen in diesem wunderbar säuerlich-süßen Eisbecher. Machen Sie genug für alle!

zeit.title: Klimaanlagen: Cool bleiben
zeit.description: Es geht heiß her: Wie findet man die richtige Klimaanlage? Fragen wir Stiftung Warentest.

zeit.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Wo nervt Sie KI?
zeit.description: Künstliche Intelligenz kann Aufgaben einfacher und Abläufe effizienter machen. Manches klappt mit ihr auch schlechter als vorher. Erzählen Sie uns, wo KI (noch) versagt.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Ukraine meldet Angriffe auf elf russische Schiffe
zeit.description: Die Ukraine hat im Asowschen Meer nach eigenen Angaben elf russische Schiffe mit Drohnen attackiert. In der Nacht gab es russische Angriffe auf Kyjiw. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: US-Einwanderungsbehörde: Tödlicher ICE-Einsatz galt offenbar anderer Person
zeit.description: Beamte der US-Einwanderungsbehörde ICE haben im Bundesstaat Maine einen 26-jährigen Kolumbianer getötet. Nach Angaben des Senators von Maine war er nicht der Gesuchte.

zeit.title: Niedersachsen: Brandanschlag legt Zugverkehr zwischen Hamburg und Cuxhaven lahm
zeit.description: Zwischen Hamburg und Cuxhaven ist der Zugverkehr derzeit unterbrochen. Grund dafür ist der Brand eines Verteilerkastens. Die Polizei geht von Brandstiftung aus.

nzz.title: Nach Schüssen in Regensdorf: Mann lässt sich von Polizei festnehmen
nzz.description: Am frühen Dienstagmorgen meldete mehrere Anwohner Schüsse. Danach versuchte die Zürcher Kantonspolizei, mit dem eingeschlossenen Schützen Kontakt aufzunehmen. Nun hat sich der Mann gestellt. In Winterthur

nzz.title: Hydration Break bei der Fussball-WM: Ist sie wirklich nötig?
nzz.description: Können Fussballer wirklich nicht 45 Minuten durchspielen, ohne zu trinken?

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Schweiz erwartet Abkühlung mit Gewittern +++ Massiver Waldbrand in der Nähe von Paris
nzz.description: Wo ist es derzeit besonders heiss? Und welche sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Hier sind die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa zu finden.

nzz.title: Der ehemalige Schweizer Nationalgoalie Yann Sommer wechselt zum FC Brügge
nzz.description: Der 37-Jährige unterschreibt beim belgischen Meister einen Dreijahresvertrag. Sein Vertrag bei Inter Mailand war zuvor ausgelaufen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Zwei Tote nach israelischen Angriffen
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Die ICE-Beamten nehmen wieder deutlich mehr Ausländer fest – nun haben sie in Texas und Maine einen Mexikaner und einen Kolumbianer erschossen
nzz.description: Das Ministerium für Inlandsicherheit sagt, der Tod eines illegal in den USA lebenden mexikanischen Kleinunternehmers sei die Folge einer Verwechslung gewesen. Die mexikanische Regierung kündigt rechtliche Schritte an.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Schweizer Wettbewerbshüter ermitteln gegen Google +++ Open AI schränkt nach Verlangen der US-Regierung Zugang zu neuer KI ein
ERKLÄRT - Schatten, Schatten, Schatten: wie man mit kleinen Kindern gut durch die Hitze kommt
nzz.description: Wie erkennt man einen Sonnenstich? Und warum sollte man den Kinderwagen nicht zudecken? Ein Kindernotfallmediziner erklärt, worauf man in der Hitze bei Kleinkindern achten muss.

nzz.title: Die britische Anti-Terror-Polizei übernimmt die Ermittlungen im Fall der tot aufgefundenen Brexit-Politikerin Ann Widdecombe
nzz.description: Die ehemalige Ministerin und Unterhausabgeordnete ist am Donnerstag leblos in ihrem Haus aufgefunden worden. Die Umstände ihres Todes sind rätselhaft.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: England gegen Argentinien ist ein Risikospiel +++ In Oslo empfangen 90'000 Menschen Erling Haaland
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Kiew greift russische Raffinerie nahe dem Uralgebirge an +++ Koalition der Willigen formiert eine einsatzbereite Truppe für die Ukraine
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Trump fordert jetzt Gebühren für die Strasse von Hormuz ein: Iran und die USA steuern auf die nächste Eskalation zu
nzz.description: Das Weisse Haus reklamiert Abgaben in Höhe von 20 Prozent aller beförderten Fracht für sich. Das Geld könnte der Präsident noch gebrauchen, denn der Kongress stemmt sich gegen die weitere Finanzierung des Krieges.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Mehr Freiheit am Sonntag – warum die Schweiz beim Ladenschluss liberaler werden muss
nzz.description: Die Schweiz reguliert im Detailhandel an den Realitäten und an den Konsumenten vorbei. Sogar Frankreich zeigt sich bei den Sonntagsverkäufen flexibler.

nzz.title: Das Rätsel um Freedom Fuel: Wer versorgt die Amerikaner plötzlich mit billigem Benzin?
nzz.description: Eine kleine Tankstellenkette hat ihre Preise gesenkt, und der Präsident ist voll des Lobes. Seine Gegner vermuteten bereits Trump selbst hinter der Aktion; die Wahrheit könnte indes viel simpler sein.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Syrien hat jetzt ein Parlament. Von einer Demokratie ist das Land aber weit entfernt
nzz.description: In den meisten arabischen Ländern dienen Parlamente nur dazu, Autokraten die Macht zu sichern. Auch das neue Syrien unter Sharaa ist bis anhin nur eine Scheindemokratie.

nzz.title: Medtech-Produkte: Die Schweiz hat in den Zollverhandlungen mit den USA einen Penalty verschenkt
nzz.description: Bern hätte den Amerikanern in einem Bereich rasch Zugeständnisse machen können: bei der Zulassung von amerikanischer Medizinaltechnik in der Schweiz. Doch es gibt Bremser innerhalb der Bundesverwaltung.

observador.title: Norwegian com prejuízo de 82 milhões de euros até junho
observador.description: Apesar do aumento de volume de negócios e total de passageiros, a companhia aérea teve prejuízo equivalente a 82 milhões de euros. Despesas extraordinárias e aumento de preços são a justificação.

observador.title: Hospitalização domiciliária evita 3.880 dias de internamento
observador.description: A hospitalização domiciliária no Hospital de Cascais teve início em 2024 com cinco camas. Atualmente têm 35 e pretende atingir as 45 até ao final deste ano.

observador.title: PS preocupado com detenção de Domingos Santos Pereira
observador.description: PS recorda os "profundos laços históricos de amizade e cooperação que unem Portugal e a Guiné-Bissau". Líder do PAIGC foi detido na sexta-feira por suspeitas de envolvimento no golpe militar de 2025.

observador.title: Observador volta a liderar o ranking de ouvintes semanais
observador.description: Em junho, os podcasts do Observador registaram mais de 2,3 milhões de downloads e ocuparam nove dos primeiros 30 lugares do ranking nacional.

observador.title: "Exames não têm sido encarados pelo ministro de forma séria"
observador.description: Mara Lagriminha, ex-deputada do PS, critica o Governo no planeamento e organização dos exames nacionais. A socialista defende ainda a presidência de António José Seguro.

observador.title: O 7-1, a melhor versão de James e a moda dos sprays
observador.description: Enquanto Brasil recolhia corações, Alemanha destruía sonhos, ao mesmo tempo que a Argentina, silenciosa, fazia o seu caminho. Portugal, como em outros Mundiais fora da Europa, ficou fora das decisões.

observador.title: Banguecoque. Negligência é a principal linha de investigação
observador.description: Polícia tailandesa está a investigar incêndio em bar. Maioria das vítimas – 30, segundo o último balanço – morreu na casa de banho. Bar pediu desculpa publicamente pelo "trágico acidente".

observador.title: Prisão preventiva para suspeito de violação e violência
observador.description: Homem de 27 anos fica em prisão preventiva pelos crimes de violação, violência doméstica e violação de domicílio contra a ex-namorada. Os crimes ocorreram na noite de quarta para quinta-feira.

observador.title: UE adota formalmente acordo comercial com México
observador.description: Acordo assinado em maio foi esta terça-feira adotado. Reduz barreiras ao comércio para empresas europeias que exportam para o México. Entrará em vigor no próximo mês de agosto.

observador.title: Lucro da Ericsson cai 44% no primeiro semestre
observador.description: Lucros registaram queda de 44% comparativamente a 2025. Segundo a Ericsson, o resultado foi afetado negativamente pelos encargos de reestruturação. CEO quer tirar proveito da "onda" de IA.

observador.title: 550 mil motas fiscalizadas. Quase 12.500 infrações detetadas
observador.description: Mais de 550 mil motociclos e condutores foram fiscalizados nos últimos sete dias nos distritos de Faro, Leiria e Setúbal, tendo sido registadas 12.429 infrações rodoviárias.

observador.title: Aguiar-Branco dá sequência a queixa da IL contra Ventura
observador.description: Aguiar-Branco remete para a Comissão Parlamentar de Transparência e Estatuto dos Deputados a queixa apresentada pela IL contra André Ventura, na sequência de um video publicado nas redes sociais.

observador.title: Onda de calor provocou pelo menos 14 mil mortos na Europa
observador.description: Nos seis países mais atingidos pela onda de calor (França, Bélgica, Alemanha, Espanha, Países Baixos e Reino Unido), morreram mais 14 mil pessoas do que seria expectável para a altura do ano.

observador.title: Mette-Marit recebe alta hospitalar
observador.description: A princesa vai passar por um período de reabilitação de seis meses, mas os médicos prevêem um ano até que a condição de saúde da mulher de Haakon possa ser considerada "estável".

observador.title: Matosinhos. Escola contra abate de árvore no recreio
observador.description: A direção da escola e a associação de pais contactaram a Câmara Municipal tentando sensibilizá-la para a manutenção da árvore. A autarquia diz que a remoção da árvore é uma medida de segurança.

observador.title: Mostra de Jovens Criadores de Teatro arranca na Amadora
observador.description: A 9ª edição conta com oito espetáculos, entre 15 e 19 de julho, com temas variados como as relações humanas, a curiosidade, a chacina, o lugar do artista e a utopia da vida adulta.

observador.title: Pacto Climático pede a municípios que protejam populações
observador.description: Embaixadora do Pacto Climático Europeu afirmou que "Portugal é um dos países europeus mais vulneráveis aos incêndios florestais". Responsáveis reconhecem "papel indispensável" das autarquias.

observador.title: E se um saco pudesse fazer a diferença?
observador.description: Eles são os nossos melhores amigos. Nós somos tudo o que lhes importa. Mas nem sempre o sabemos retribuir. Saiba como fazer a diferença na vida dos amigos de quatro patas, com um simples saco.

spiegel.title: Italien: Neue Regeln legen hunderte Blitzer vorübergehend lahm
spiegel.description: Angesichts neuer Vorschriften sind viele Tempomessgeräte in Italien außer Betrieb. Für sie müssen die Hersteller nun eine Zertifizierung beantragen. Ein Verbraucherverband begrüßt die Regelungen.

spiegel.title: Jeffrey Hood, Seelsorger im Todestrakt: Wie ein Priester Verurteilte begleitet
spiegel.description: Der Priester Jeffrey Hood spricht jeden Tag mit Mördern und Vergewaltigern, die zum Tode verurteilt sind. Das bringt den Familienvater um den Schlaf. Warum will er trotzdem bis zum letzten Atemzug bei ihnen sein?

spiegel.title: Gardasee: Deutscher stirbt bei Absturz mit Gleitschirm
spiegel.description: Ein Paragliding-Ausflug am Gardasee endete für einen 61-jährigen Deutschen tödlich. Seit Juni gab es in der Region bereits drei solcher Unglücksfälle.

spiegel.title: USA unter Donald Trump: »Niemand verdient es, auf der Straße erschossen zu werden«
spiegel.description: Viele Details sind noch unklar, doch schon wieder gibt es in den USA einen Todesfall im Zusammenhang mit ICE-Beamten. Ein Überwachungsvideo zeigt, wie Beamte einen Mann aus einem Auto zerren.

spiegel.title: Nordrhein-Westfalen und Rheinland-Pfalz: Polizei durchsucht JVA Rheinbach und mehrere Wohnungen
spiegel.description: Mitarbeitende der JVA Rheinberg sollen nach SPIEGEL-Informationen unter Verdacht stehen, an Drogenschmuggel beteiligt gewesen zu sein. Kürzlich wurde ein ähnlicher Fall in Nordrhein-Westfalen bekannt.

spiegel.title: RAF: Opferfamilien unterstützen Wunsch nach zentraler Gedenkstätte
spiegel.description: Bayerns Innenminister Herrmann will ein Mahnmal für die Opfer des RAF-Terrors. Der Sohn von Hanns Martin Schleyer findet: »Es wird höchste Zeit«.

spiegel.title: Iran greift US-Stützpunkte in Jordanien, VAE und an
spiegel.description: Auf die US-Angriffe in der Nacht reagiert Iran mit umfangreichen Luftangriffen. Außenminister Abbas Araghchi antwortet zudem auf Donald Trumps Seeblockade.

spiegel.title: Fairer Handel: Deutsche geben weniger dafür aus als europäische Nachbarn
spiegel.description: Die Branche zieht eine gemischte Bilanz: Die Umsätze mit fair gehandeltem Kaffee oder Schokolade sind 2025 zwar gestiegen. Doch im Vergleich zu Österreich oder Frankreich ist bei den Deutschen deutlich Luft nach oben.

spiegel.title: Gaby Köster ist nach Schlaganfall dankbar für Helfer im Alltag
spiegel.description: Die Schauspielerin Gaby Köster berichtet, dass sie nach ihrem Schlaganfall auf die Hilfe von Mitmenschen angewiesen ist. Die Pflegestufe reiche nicht aus. Dann teilt sie aus: gegen Politiker, die Behandlung von Pflegekräften und die AfD.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Andy Burnham ist der Labour-Vorsitz (fast) nicht mehr zu nehmen
spiegel.description: Erst Bürgermeister in Manchester, bald wohl Premier: Labour-Politiker Andy Burnham liegt im Rennen um die Nachfolge von Parteichef Keir Starmer uneinholbar vorn. Mit dem Machtwechsel könnte es nun schnell gehen.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Pilot schreibt »mir ist langweilig« in den Himmel
spiegel.description: Zweieinhalb Stunden ist ein Mann mit einem Leichtflugzeug durch die Gegend geflogen, um ein ausgetauschtes Teil zu testen. Wie seine Route zeigt, war das wohl ziemlich öde.

spiegel.title: A7 in Schleswig-Holstein: Frau bringt Baby auf Rastplatz zur Welt
spiegel.description: Der Junge hatte es offenbar besonders eilig: Eine Frau war auf dem Weg ins Krankenhaus, als die Geburt einsetzte – statt in der Klinik kam das Kind auf dem Rastplatz Brokenlande zur Welt.

spiegel.title: Minijobs: So ließen sie sich am sinnvollsten reformieren
spiegel.description: Die schwarz-rote Koalition ist gefordert: Experten pochen auf das weitgehende Ende der Minijobs – auf die jedoch Millionen Bürger angewiesen sind. Wie eine sinnvolle Reform aussehen könnte.

spiegel.title: ESA: Astronaut Matthias Maurer übt Zähne ziehen
spiegel.description: Im All einen Arzt zu finden, dürfte schwierig sein. Für den Ernstfall müssen Astronauten also ein medizinisches Training absolvieren. Matthias Maurer sagt, er habe beim Zähneziehen mehr gelitten als seine Übungspatienten.

spiegel.title: Heidelberg: Behördenmitarbeiter soll Frau sexuell genötigt haben
spiegel.description: Schwere Vorwürfe gegen einen Behördenmitarbeiter in Baden-Württemberg: Er soll von einer Frau sexuelle Dienste verlangt und dafür versprochen haben, ihre Abschiebung zu verhindern. Inzwischen gibt es weitere Verdachtsfälle.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Argentinische Veteranen wollen Falkland-Krieg aus Halbfinale gegen England heraushalten
spiegel.description: Das Duell zwischen England und Argentinien ist auch wegen der gemeinsamen Geschichte beider Länder brisant. phys-org.title: Research brings the era of microbial cell factories one step closer
phys-org.description: The era of "biomanufacturing," in which microbes, not petroleum, produce chemical products, is one step closer. A KAIST research team has analyzed the key challenges limiting the commercialization of biomanufacturing and proposed an AI-driven strategy for industrialization.

phys-org.title: How the built environment can help protect mental health in a changing climate
phys-org.description: When people think about climate change, they often picture melting glaciers, stronger storms, rising temperatures, or prolonged droughts. These visible consequences dominate headlines and shape public discussions. Yet another consequence is quietly growing in the background—one that cannot be measured with a thermometer or satellite image. Climate change is increasingly affecting how people think, feel, and imagine their future.

phys-org.title: No relief from the heat as many US cities will see record overnight temperatures
phys-org.description: Another week of blistering heat will bring even more health risks in the coming days, as overnight temperatures won't provide much relief.

phys-org.title: Unequal taxation helped fuel the French Revolution, say economists
phys-org.description: Deep inequalities in taxation played a key role in fueling the French Revolution, according to a new study published by the ROCKWOOL Foundation Berlin (RFBerlin). For the first time, economists have substantiated this with figures. In areas where salt taxes and internal customs duties were particularly high, there were twice as many revolts as in low-tax districts between 1750 and 1789.

phys-org.title: Supportive supervisors lift performance for employees with disabilities, study finds
phys-org.description: Supportive supervisors can improve the performance of employees with disabilities, according to research in the International Journal of Business Innovation and Research. However, the broader workplace environment determines how much that support translates into results.

phys-org.title: Most of the moon's water likely remains chemically bound in its deep interior
phys-org.description: After decades of analyzing reams of lunar rocks back here on Earth, the canonical view of the moon was that it was anhydrous; that it had extraordinarily little water. That all began to change in 2009 with new data from NASA's Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) and the much-ballyhooed evidence of water ice in the moon's permanently shaded polar regions (PSRs).

phys-org.title: Typhoons mix up bacteria and biochemistry
phys-org.description: After a typhoon surprised a research cruise, scientists took advantage of the unique sampling opportunity to reveal rapid changes in bacterioplankton communities and biogeochemical cycling.

phys-org.title: How redefining one word strips the Endangered Species Act's ability to protect vital habitat
phys-org.description: It wouldn't make much sense to prohibit people from shooting a threatened woodpecker while allowing its forest to be cut down, or to bar killing endangered salmon while allowing a dam to dry out their habitat.

phys-org.title: Dead stars in our cosmic backyard: Astronomers spot four white dwarfs hiding under our noses
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Warwick and the University of Colorado Boulder have directly observed, for the first time, four white dwarfs in binary star systems in our nearby region of space. These stellar binaries are all within 65 light-years of Earth, and one contains the ninth-closest white dwarf to the sun.

phys-org.title: Hidden in Maya wall writings: A named astronomer emerges from 1,200-year-old calculations
phys-org.description: Researchers have reconstructed and transcribed a mathematical formula from the site of Xultun, Guatemala, revealing the name of a Maya astronomer for the first time. During the Classic period (250–900 CE), mathematics and astronomy were a key part of Maya society, with complex calculations based on calendar dates and astronomical observations influencing everything from the erection of monuments to the inauguration of kings and queens.

phys-org.title: Climate disclosure gives Canadian companies an edge with European investors, new research shows
phys-org.description: Canadian companies that disclose their climate-related risks and impacts have a considerable advantage over those that don't when it comes to attracting financing from European institutional investors, according to our recent report for the Institute for Sustainable Finance at Queen's University.

phys-org.title: Teachers are worried about students cheating with AI, but my survey suggests the deeper issue is learning
phys-org.description: The risk of students using AI to cheat tends to get a lot of attention—with good reason.

phys-org.title: Floating-electron catalyst withstands week in air while making ammonia under milder conditions
phys-org.description: A surface electrene, BaSiN2:O, developed by researchers at Science Tokyo enables efficient ammonia synthesis under mild conditions while overcoming the long-standing air instability of electrene materials. Synthesized by doping barium silicon nitride with oxygen, the material forms a stable layer of freely floating electrons on its surface.

phys-org.title: Carbon storage could curb more than 90% of AI data center emissions, study finds
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence accelerates demand for computing power across the U.S., a new study co-authored by Hon Chung Lau, adjunct professor in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at Rice University and founder of Low Carbon Energies LLC, has found that carbon capture and storage could play a major role in limiting the climate impact of data centers.

phys-org.title: Scientists uncover molecular mechanism linking water-saving irrigation to cadmium accumulation in rice
phys-org.description: Water-saving irrigation practices, including intermittent irrigation, are essential for sustainable rice cultivation amid growing freshwater shortages. However, periodic drainage creates aerobic soil conditions that drastically boost cadmium (Cd) bioavailability, leading to severe grain Cd enrichment. Disentangling the relationship between water conservation and high grain Cd has been a critical challenge for rice breeders and soil scientists worldwide.

phys-org.title: AI-powered electronic nose can distinguish tens of thousands of odors
phys-org.description: A research team has presented a roadmap for developing an "artificial olfactory system" that detects odors like the human nose and analyzes them using artificial intelligence (AI) by leveraging metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). The team systematically organized and reviewed key research trends in electronic nose technology, from MOF material design to sensor implementation and AI-based odor pattern recognition. The research was led by Hyuk-Jun Kwon's in the Department of Electrical Engineeri

phys-org.title: Hundreds of economists say 'we must act now' on AI's economic impact and job displacement risks
phys-org.description: Hundreds of economists say in an open letter that institutions "must act now" to address how artificial intelligence could transform the economy and could put many people out of work.

phys-org.title: Where mainshocks strike may explain earthquake size patterns better than timing, data suggests
phys-org.description: Japan is well known for its large earthquakes, but not all regions show the same patterns of earthquake activity. One way to understand which places tend to experience large or small earthquakes is the b-value, a key statistical measure long used by researchers to understand seismicity and assess earthquake occurrence patterns.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.
